title: Zephyrine and the Thorn
premise: Theo Eriksen keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories and impossible goods, hiding behind a genderless name and a talent for being forgotten. When a prophecy written a century ago names 'the thief who is no one' as the key to reopening a door out of Zephyrine—a country erased from every map after a coup that officially never happened—Theo becomes hunted by both the guild that raised them and the regime that wants the prophecy buried. To find the door, Theo must gather a found family of prophecy-marked strangers, including Wren, a knight sworn to arrest them, whose love forces both to choose between duty and each other. In the end Theo trades their own memories of everyone they love to open the door, saving the country's exiles while keeping only one thing: a blank page where Wren's face should be—and Wren chooses to stay behind in the erased country to write their story back into existence.
about_author: Tamsin Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing confiscated books in a coastal city that has changed its name three times. They write fantasy about people the records forgot, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A night of routine thefts: a widow's grief, a general's shame, all entered neatly in the Vellum Guild's ledgers. Theo establishes the rules of their invisibility—never be remembered, never be named. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cataloguing a looted library, Theo finds a century-old prophecy book listing tonight's exact date beside a description of themselves. The guildmaster, Sable, goes pale and orders the page burned. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of an ordinary life.

chapters.title: What the Guild Does to Loose Ends
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo learns the last person named in the prophecy was 'retired' by the guild forty years ago. They steal their own ledger page and flee into the Ashmarket. Emotional beat: betrayal by the only family they've known.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Forgets Nothing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Eriksen-adjacent? No—Wren Aldous, a knight of the Provisional Authority, is assigned to find the prophecy-thief. Unlike everyone else, Wren's memory cannot be stolen, making her the perfect hunter. Emotional beat: dutiful certainty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Ashmarket Bargains
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Hiding among black-market memory dealers, Theo meets Pip, a child pickpocket who can taste lies, and buys passage on a smuggler's barge using a stolen memory of the sea. Emotional beat: first fragile alliance outside the guild.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the barge, smuggler Odile explains Zephyrine's erasure: conquered, renamed, its borders redrawn; the old country survives only in contraband maps and the prophecy. Emotional beat: grief for a homeland Theo never knew they had.

chapters.title: First Blood at the Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren corners Theo at a river tollhouse but hesitates when Theo shows her the prophecy naming them both. She lets them go—an act of treason she now must hide. Emotional beat: duty and doubt at knifepoint.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Seeking the last mapmaker who drew Zephyrine's true borders, Theo finds instead his daughter Isolde, who guards his final unfinished map and resents prophecy-marked strangers. Emotional beat: learning that being chosen by fate is not the same as being wanted.

chapters.title: Sable's Offer
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The guildmaster catches up and offers Theo absolution: return the ledger pages, forget everything, resume invisibility. Theo refuses for the first time in their life. Emotional beat: choosing a self over a survival strategy.

chapters.title: What Wren Buried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback chapter: Wren's brother was disappeared by the Authority for asking about Zephyrine. Her flawless memory is both gift and wound. Emotional beat: understanding why she hunts—for control over what remembering costs.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Map
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Isolde agrees to finish the map if they recover her father's stolen memory of it from a guild vault. The found family plans its first heist together. Emotional beat: tentative trust becoming something like love.

chapters.title: Heist in the House of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The vault job goes wrong; Sable anticipated them. Pip is captured, and Theo must choose between the map fragment and the child. They choose Pip. Emotional beat: the cost of family made concrete.

chapters.title: Half a Border
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. With half the map recovered, Isolde reveals the door out of Zephyrine requires more than geography—it requires a sacrifice of memory, which is why the guild hoards them. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Authority Closes In
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's superior suspects her treason and sends her to capture the thieves or be disappeared like her brother. She defects, burning her commission, and finds Theo's camp at dawn. Emotional beat: love declared through ruin.

chapters.title: Interlude: One Night Without Running
chapters.summary: Theo and Wren's alternating POV. A quiet chapter: shared stories, an argument about whether forgetting is mercy or death, and a kiss neither can promise to remember. Emotional beat: tenderness under a countdown.

chapters.title: The Price of the Door
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The full mechanism revealed: the door opens only for someone who gives up every memory tying them to the world—the ultimate erasure, mirroring Zephyrine's own. Theo volunteers before anyone can object. Emotional beat: horror and awe at the symmetry.

chapters.title: Sable's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Final confrontation with Sable at the border ruins; Sable confesses she was the prophecy's previous candidate and chose the guild over the door, and has regretted it for forty years. She lets them pass. Emotional beat: pity replacing hatred.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Climax, ensemble POV. At the border ruins, pursued by the Authority, Theo pays the price: memories stripped one by one as the door grinds open. Wren holds their hand and tells them, repeatedly, 'My name is Wren.' Emotional beat: devastating sacrifice.

chapters.title: Exodus
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The exiles cross into the restored Zephyrine—but Wren stays on the threshold, unable to enter a home built on Theo's forgetting. The door begins to close. Emotional beat: love refusing the easy ending.

chapters.title: The Blank Page
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the far side, Theo wakes whole but hollowed, holding a ledger with one blank page where Wren should be. Pip and Isolde refuse to let the erasure stand. Emotional beat: grief without an object, hope without proof.

chapters.title: Written Back Into Existence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren remains in the erased country, writing Zephyrine's true history into the prophecy book itself, restoring the nation word by word—and writing Theo back across the border, because a story told truly enough becomes a door. Emotional beat: devotion as authorship.

chapters.title: Zephyrine and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Theo's POV. The door reopens; Wren steps through into a remembered country, and Theo—who kept one stolen memory hidden even from the door—says her name first. The found family builds a new guild: one that returns what was taken. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, love against duty, both kept.
